name: Spinner
description: A continuously spinning loader that signals an indeterminate wait — an action in progress or a region still loading. It comes in three sizes (sm / md / lg), takes its color from the foreground token, and exposes an accessible "Loading" status to assistive technology.
whenToUse: Signal that an action is in progress — a button submitting, a panel fetching
Fill a region that is still loading when you can't show real content yet
whenNotToUse: Showing how far along a known task is — use a determinate progress bar
Long or content-heavy loads where a skeleton better previews the layout

size.sm: 16px — inline with text or inside a small control like a button.
size.md: 24px — default, for standalone or region-level loading.
size.lg: 32px — prominent, for full-panel or page-level waits.

states.default: Continuously animating (spinning) — the spinner has no resting or interactive states.

dos: Give the spinner an accessible label so screen readers announce the wait
Match the size to its context — small inside controls, larger for regions
Pair a longer wait with a short message so users know what's happening
donts: Don't use a spinner for progress you can actually measure
Don't leave a spinner running with no resolution or timeout
Don't rely on the spin alone — expose a text status for assistive tech

keyboard: Not interactive and not focusable — it conveys status only
notes: Wrapper carries role="status" with an aria-label (defaults to "Loading")
The spinning glyph is aria-hidden so only the status text is announced
role="status" announces politely without stealing focus
